summary: Naresh Keerthi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2018–2021) and was appointed Assistant Professor at Ashoka University in 2021.

Nariaki Nakazato is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta in 1985. He held posts at the Toyo Bunko, Kobe University, and the University of Tokyo (professor, ~1996–2011).
Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Taisho University, attested in 1974 and 1988.

Nashalla Gwyn Nyinda works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Naropa University, Chagpori Tibetan Medical Institute, Shang Shung Institute, Qinghai University, and ITEA. She became Clinic Director at Nyinda Clinic (2009) and President of Chagpori Tibetan Medical Institute (2022).

Natalie Depraz is a philosopher educated at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre University. She held professorships at the University of Rouen Normandy and Paris Nanterre University, and a research post at the University of Bucharest (2023–2026).

Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She held an affiliation at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan V. Beyer. She also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lengden, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.

Natalie Quli works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied at Cal Poly Humboldt and the Graduate Theological Union. She holds the Yehan Numata Professorship of Buddhist Studies at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan (1999–2006). She joined the faculty at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natalya Julianovna Lubotskaya (1933–1985) was an Indologist. She studied at Moscow State Pedagogical University (~1950–1955) and served as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1957 to 1976.

Natalya Mikhailovna Sazanova (1932–2006) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied history at Moscow State University (~1949–1954), where she taught beginning in 1958 and became a professor in 1989.

Natalya Vasilyevna Dyakonova (1907–1996) studied at Saint Petersburg State University. Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and Buddhist studies, she held posts at the Ukrainian Oriental Institute, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the State Hermitage Museum.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She held appointments at UC Berkeley, UCLA (attested 2016), and the University of Virginia (Associate Professor, 2017).

Natasha Reichle is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Alan Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.

Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen (~2011–2018) under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker. She also held a post at the University of Groningen, attested in 2013.
Nathan Brown (1807–1886) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Japanology. He studied at Williams College and Newton Theological Institution, and founded the American Baptist Missionary Union in 1837.
Nathan Sivin (1931–2022) was a Sinologist and historian educated at MIT and Harvard. He taught at MIT from 1966 to 1977 and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from 1977 to 2006.

Nathan Söderblom (1866–1931) studied at Uppsala University, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE, specializing in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He was a professor of history of religion at Uppsala (1901–1912) and Leipzig (1912–1914).

Nathan W. Hill is a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He held positions at SOAS (2008–2019), Trinity College Dublin (from 2019), and NYU (2024).

Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was an Indologist and linguist who was educated at Harrow School and Christ Church. He served as an official for the East India Company (~1771–1785) and as secretary at East India House (1809).
